clue.text: Excellent rent, highly profitable

parts.note: a rent is a tear, as is a rip
a business doing a roaring trade is highly profitable

explanation.surface: A landlord gloats over a lucrative rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but here it is a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean boisterously splendid, a colloquial synonym for first-rate.

clue.text: Wander to other side of river going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter travelling north moves up from the bottom to the top of the word

parts.note: going over a bridge takes you to the other side

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses a river heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the end of OVER climbs to the top in this down entry, giving R then OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander without fixed course; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Run fast and hide

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to run at speed

explanation.definitionFit: Pelting means rushing; a pelt is also an animal skin, a fur.

clue.text: Expect too much of single male in laird's position

indicators.note: the letters for single male are put inside the laird's position

parts.note: a laird, a Scottish landowner, is placed over his estate
I is the Roman numeral one, so single

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner's bachelor heir is burdened with high hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor; his position is 'over estate', which takes IM inside to give ESTIMATE after OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something too highly is to expect more of it than it can deliver.

clue.text: Arrive with expedition and get arrested

definitions.meaning: expedition here means speed, so to arrive quickly is to come running in
being taken to the police station is informally being ...

explanation.definitionFit: Running in is coming in at speed; police slang also uses it for taking someone into custody.

clue.text: Careless fellow with broken leg in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the jumbled leg sits between the two letters for Northern Ireland
a broken limb is out of shape, so the letters of leg are rearranged

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in Ulster has fractured his leg through carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the leg's letters to EGL, and 'in' puts them between the two letters for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent describes someone failing to take proper care, so heedless or careless.

clue.text: Help a Yankee, perhaps

parts.note: a Yankee is a type of accumulator wager placed with bookmakers, so an example of a bet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an American visitor needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is a British betting term: four selections combined in eleven bets. 'Yankee' looks like an American.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone, usually in wrongdoing, is to assist them.

clue.text: Foreign beauty's source of drug

definitions.meaning: in Italian ... means a beautiful lady
deadly nightshade, the plant that yields atropine

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means fair lady; it also names deadly nightshade, a plant from which atropine is extracted.

clue.text: Was apt to go round upward slope, being less tough

indicators.note: the verb tense for was apt encircles the slope, holding it inside

parts.note: if one tended to do something one was apt to do it
a rise is ground that slopes upward

explanation.surface: Something inclined to circle a hill has been softened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' is the container signal; 'upward slope' is a single noun, not a reversal instruction in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that has been beaten or marinated to soften it has been made more tender.

clue.text: Community restricting a German serf's status

indicators.note: the village hems in the German article, holding it inside

parts.note: a village is a small rural community
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A rural settlement confines a German labourer to bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' is the container signal: the community holds the German word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A villein was a feudal serf, and villeinage his tenure or condition of bondage.

clue.text: Social group, sound as a bell, but no good

indicators.note: but no here means without, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a bell rings with a clang

explanation.surface: A gathering sounds fine but proves useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like an idiom for healthy; it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of families sharing descent, a social unit.

clue.text: It preserves notes penned by starchy alter ego

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the notes are shut inside the other pieces

parts.note: starchy behaviour is stiff and formal
Mr Hyde is the alter ego of Dr Jekyll
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: Music is written down by a stiff man's hidden other self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' means shut in. Hyde is the evil other self of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical, in solution as formalin, is used to keep biological specimens from decay.

clue.text: Check price on port in Spain and provide new refreshment

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another follows it, so the price comes after the port

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Vigo is a port in Galicia, Spain
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: Someone checks a Spanish port's charges before restocking drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To give fresh energy to something is to revive or refresh it once more.

clue.text: Brief note makes house tremble

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour
to quaver is to tremble, especially of a voice

explanation.surface: A short message is enough to make a home shake.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is British for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a sixteenth note, of short duration in music.

clue.text: Lists of supplementary material and piano pieces, perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: Lists of supplementary material and piano pieces, perhaps: 'and piano pieces, perhaps' gives no letters or second sense I can parse; possibly OCR-damaged.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lists of supplementary material and piano pieces, perhaps

clue.text: Emotionally identify English politician, at his office at last

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word office

explanation.surface: An English MP is at his desk at the end of the day, feeling sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel what another feels is to share their feelings, an emotional identification.

clue.text: Bring in a set of books of great significance

parts.note: to import goods is to bring them in from abroad
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Bringing in a collection of volumes matters greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set of books' looks like a library; it is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty or consequential is significant.

clue.text: Girl mostly comprehends old Polynesian language

indicators.note: comprehends means takes in, so the girl's name holds the letter inside
mostly means most of the name, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl largely understands an ancient Pacific tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the girl's last letter, leaving MARI; 'comprehends' then takes the old letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous people of New Zealand speak a Polynesian tongue of that name.

clue.text: Part of intestine or pelvic bone, say

indicators.note: say signals that the bone's name is spoken, giving a word pronounced the same

parts.note: the ilium is the broad upper bone of the pelvis

explanation.surface: An anatomy student confuses a gut section with a hip bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The two anatomical terms are pronounced alike but spelt with I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Favourite weapon to contain union leader's peevishness

indicators.note: the favourite and weapon together hold the leading letter between them

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
a lance is a long spear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss holds a favourite spear in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' means the favourite and the weapon side by side hold the union's leading letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky ill temper, the same as irritable peevishness.

clue.text: Name home in a French document? It's not settled

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the name and home are put inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
to term something is to name it
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A French deed names a house, but the matter remains unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts name and home inside the document; 'Name' is the verb, to call.
explanation.definitionFit: An open question has not been decided, so it is undetermined.

clue.text: Man, for example, securing employment ultimately as rope-maker?

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the isle encloses the letter

parts.note: the Isle of Man is one example of an isle

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of employment

explanation.surface: A man ties down a job at last as a ropemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man; 'securing' holds the job's final letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre used for cord and rope, so a material that makes rope, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Way 'in which lake adjoins bay

parts.note: how means the way in which something is done

explanation.surface: A coastal path where a lake meets a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like the sea inlet; it is the verb, as a hound bays.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's long cry is a howl, which is what baying means.

clue.text: It's still all right without an affirmative vote

definitions.text: It's still all right without an affirmative vote

parts.words: It's still all right without an affirmative vote
parts.note: the word means all right, and taking away the two letters of a yes vote leaves the shorter two-letter word with the same meaning

explanation.definitionFit: It is the full spelling of the casual approval word, synonymous with fine or acceptable.

clue.text: Immoral conduct of counsel disposing of notice

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so the notice is removed

parts.note: counsel is advice
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Legal counsel throws away a notice amid allegations of misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counsel' looks like a barrister; it means advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice is wickedness, depraved or immoral behaviour.

clue.text: Baker found former transport firm satisfactory

parts.note: past means former, gone by
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A baker turns out to be a one-time haulage company that was fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport firm' reads as one company, but splits into railway and company abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry cook makes pies and cakes, a kind of baker.

clue.text: Baby food king's son consumed in this state

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed up inside, so the son sits within the state

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, the state where the clue appears

explanation.surface: A royal heir is eaten up in the kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a hard dry biscuit given to teething infants.

clue.text: English article actually written in airy way

parts.note: the is the definite article
really means actually, in fact

explanation.surface: An English essay is written in a light, dreamy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing; it is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light and airy, delicate as if not of this world.
